title: Resistance to change
log: 2026-10-27T01:00:11Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers why people resist change; the closest ones are about the business environment and life cycle, which are different ideas.

draft.title: Resistance to change
card: Resistance to change is when people in a business oppose or delay a change. It can come from employees, managers or others affected, and it can slow a change down or stop it.
People may resist because the change costs them time, effort or money, or because they fear the unknown and are unsure what it will mean for their job.
People may resist because they could lose status or influence, or because they are used to the current way of working and prefer it.
If staff are not told what is changing and why, they may fill the gap with rumours and doubt, and resist the change.
draft.remember: People resist change when it costs them, worries them, threatens their standing, upsets habits or is poorly explained.

a.q: A café owner brings in a new ordering app. A long-serving waiter refuses to use it and says, "The paper pads work fine." Which reason for resistance is this?
opts: Habit, as the waiter prefers the usual way of working
Lost status, as the waiter loses a senior role
Poor communication, as no one explained the app
Costs, as the waiter must pay for the app
a.why: The waiter says the old method works fine, which shows a preference for the usual way of working. Lost status is tempting, but nothing in the case says the waiter loses a role or influence.
a.clue: Look at what the waiter says about the old pads.

b.q: A factory in Newcastle plans to move to a new production system. Managers tell staff nothing until the week it starts. Many workers then say they think jobs will be cut. Which best explains their resistance?
opts: Poor communication led to fear of the unknown
Habit made the workers dislike all new systems
The workers lost status once the system started
The system cost the workers money to learn
b.why: Staff were not told what was happening, so they feared for their jobs. Habit is tempting, but the workers' concern is about job cuts, not about liking the old system. Nothing in the case says they lost status or paid costs.
b.clue: Think about what the workers were told before the change and what they feared.

a.best: Habit, as the waiter prefers the usual way of working

b.best: Poor communication led to fear of the unknown
